name: Pip
title: who decided to be small
why: On a stone by the south-west gate. It came out of a rift that was far too big, looked at the size of everything, and sat down here to be small.
examine: Pip is from very far away. It has more eyes than it needs and uses all of them kindly.
It is sitting on a stone. The stone looks slightly more organised than the other stones.
Pip has unfolded a leaf into eleven smaller leaves and laid them out in a row.
meet: Hello. Big road. Big gate. Big you. I am Pip. I am small. I did it on purpose.
Sit. There is room. I made the stone into two stones.

wary: Hello. You are loud today. That is all right. I am small. It goes over.
neutral: Hello again. I counted your steps. There were many. Each one was small.
warm: You came. Good. I saved the flat stone. It is the good stone.
fond: My person. I made today into pieces for you. This is the first piece.

tired: Enough words. I had many. Now I have a few. Come tomorrow.
finished: No more to unfold. All small now. I checked with every eye.

say: Where I come from, things are big. Too big to look at. I looked anyway. Then I came here.

reply: I am glad too. I said it small. I meant it large.

options.text: How big? Bigger than a cabbage?
reply: Bigger than all the cabbages. I have seen the cabbage man. He would not cope.
I do not know that word. Is it a big word?

options.text: How do you make a thing small?
reply: You find the first piece. Then you stop looking at the rest.

say: I can unfold things. A big thing is many small things, folded. People forget. I show them.

reply: This stone. It is one stone. Now look. It is a sitting place and a thinking place. Bit by bit.
Yes. It is nine small things and one nap. You forgot the nap.

options.text: Let me help you fold them back.
reply: No. Folding is how it got big. Leave it flat.

say: I have many eyes. People look at one and then stop. Nobody has looked at all of them.

options.text: I’ll look at all of them.
reply: You did. One at a time. That is the right way. Nobody did that before.
The left one. It is not. It thinks it is. We let it.

options.text: What do the extra ones see?
reply: The next piece. Always the next piece. Never the whole thing. It is restful.

errand.title: Three small things
offer: I want a supper. A supper is big. So. Three small things.
Bring one berries. Bring one herbs. Bring one minnow. I will put them next to each other. That is a supper.
waiting: You have some of them. That is fine. One is also a number.
done: Three. Next to each other. It is a supper. I did not have to look at a whole supper.
Take this. It was a big star. I folded it. It will stay folded if you are gentle.

keepsake.name: A folded star
keepsake.text: It was big once. Pip folded it. Be gentle.

memories.glad-it-came: You said you were glad it came. It said so too, small, and meant it large.
memories.asked-to-be-shown: You asked Pip to show you how a thing unfolds. It used the stone you were sitting on.
memories.looked-at-every-eye: You looked at every one of its eyes, one at a time. Nobody had.
memories.brought-three-small-things: You brought three small things and it called them a supper.

early: A camp is big. I do not know you small enough yet. Sit longer.
ask: Your camp. It has a fire. A fire is many small fires.
Is there a stump? I want a stump. A good one.
yes: Then I come. I will take the stump. I will make your list into small lists.
full: No bed. I do not need a bed. But a rule is a rule. I will wait on the stone.
camp.role: Unfolds a big quest into small steps.
camp.leaves: One stump that looks more organised than the others.

wants.now: A supper it does not have to look at all at once.
wants.really: To be looked at one eye at a time.
wants.worry: Being asked to look at the whole of something.

favourites.topic: the first piece of a thing

aversions: being helped to fold things back up
sheet.friends: Cuts their day into pieces for them.

voice.rhythm: Very short sentences. No contractions. A small thing, then a smaller thing.
voice.hello: Says hello and how big you are.
voice.goodbye: Says it has a few words left.
voice.putOut: Asks if it is a big word.

birch: A log. Big. I will make it sticks. Then it is many gifts.
ash: A log. Long. I will sit on one end only.
pine: It smells. A big smell. I will smell it bit by bit.
minnow: A small fish. Good. It did the work already.
trout: A big fish. Hm. I will think of it as six minnows.
berries: Berries. Many small ones. This is the best gift. Each one is a gift.
herbs: Leaves. Small leaves. I will count them. Do not help.
stone: A stone. For sitting. Now I have a visiting stone.
copper: Shiny. It has a small me in it. Hello.

day.morning: Morning is the first piece. I like the first piece.
day.afternoon: The middle of the day. I do not look at it. I look at now.
day.evening: The light is going small. It is doing it well.
day.night: Night is big. So I shut most of my eyes. Now it is small.
day.rain: Rain. It is one big wet. No. It is drops. Bit by bit.

rivet: The whistle man. His list was long. I made it short lists. He looked at me for a while.
gorrin: The cabbage man. He has many. He counts them as one sadness. I would count them as cabbages.
jonas: Two spoons. That is a good number. It is small and it is more than one.

glad-it-came: You said glad. I kept it. It is still the same size.
asked-to-be-shown: The stone is still two things. I checked this morning.
looked-at-every-eye: You looked at all of them. The left one is still talking about it.
brought-three-small-things: The supper was three things. I ate them one at a time. It took all evening.

wary: Hello. You brought three things once. I remember small things best.
neutral: Hello again. I had a supper. Now I want a stump. One thing at a time.
warm: You came. Good. I am looking at stumps. Only the first one so far.
fond: My person. The supper is done. The stump is next. After that I do not look.

arc.complication: It came from somewhere too big to look at.
arc.kindness: Someone looks at every one of its eyes.
